name: Detravex
description: Detravex is a three-day injectable protocol that chemically severs established dependency pathways by flooding mu-opioid, dopamine D2, and reinforcement-loop receptors with a competitive antagonist cascade, forcing a hard neurochemical reset. The process is notoriously brutal — patients describe it as 'feeling every high you ever had being ripped back out' — but clinical completion rates show 74% long-term abstinence for opioid and stimulant dependencies. It is administered under medical supervision with mandatory sedation support for the first 18 hours.
effects: Complete severance of established chemical dependency pathways
Receptor desensitization reset to pre-addiction baseline
Elimination of substance-specific cravings within 72 hours
Mild euphoric window on day 3 as natural dopamine rebounds
side_effects: Extreme physical pain during first 36 hours — muscle convulsions, sweating, fever
Psychological terror and intrusive memory cascade during receptor purge
Temporary emotional flatness lasting 2-4 weeks post-treatment
Rare: seizure risk in patients with BCI hardware (neural feedback loop interference)
Approximately 12% of patients require psychiatric follow-up for acute trauma responses to the purge process
duration: 72-hour active protocol; full neurochemical stabilization over 3-4 weeks
street_price: Φ1,800 for full kit (black market administered; Φ600 clinic co-pay Tier 2)
cultural_context: Detravex is the working-class 'nuclear option' — what Shelf climbers and Tier 2 laborers save up for when they want out of a hard substance spiral. Tier 3 clinics run supervised Detravex programs marketed as 'Clean Restart' packages. On the Shelf, unlicensed practitioners administer it without sedation support, which has earned it a savage reputation. The phrase 'doing the Scrape' is used as a general metaphor in GLMZ slang for any brutal but necessary act of self-destruction for future gain.
story_hooks: A Shelf enforcer is trying to get clean before a job — but the black market Detravex kit they bought is counterfeit, and whoever sold it to them doesn't want them coherent enough to testify about what they witnessed
A Novafold clinic's supervised Detravex program is being used as a cover — patients sedated for 18 hours make ideal unwitting test subjects for something else entirely
A character survives the Scrape but the intrusive memory cascade during the purge surfaces something they had chemically suppressed — not just cravings, but a memory they didn't know they had
